hints.content: The arrow points to all values less than $1$.
And the point at $1$ is filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything **less than or equal to $1$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**


[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at 1 and continues left. A closed point is plotted at 1 where the line begins.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < 1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at 1 and continues left. An open point is plotted at 1 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/3977545e176131825f917115c7d6f358e0b4266b)

The graph of $x > 1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at 1 and continues right. An open point is plotted at 1 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/9388dfaf978b768d0aad28dcbc2c547a141db518)

The graph of $x \geq 1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at 1 and continues right. A closed point is plotted at 1 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/812e1d33499f2567cc69cc7370fa6acda6aff43c)
